In dimensions N≥3 the centered bound uses R=N−J+1. Hadamard bounds the determinant squared by the product of squared row norms, each at most m_i s_i. The product of row sums is at most one by AM–GM. All maxima are at most one, and there are R factors at or below the Jth largest, yielding the exact second threshold.

The comparison costs at an eligible point have strict positive margin by r+max_i(b_i−b)_+<δ and W_i≤2. Integrating the pointwise multiplicity does not require a fixed set of good indices. The min over tilts is attained by continuity and exact saturation at large absolute tilts.

For d≥2 the positive second-order binomial term in (1+1/d)^d gives strict excess over two, so J/N≥1/2>Γ_d. Exact rational checks verified that strict comparison for d up to 99 and the interval row-maxima identity on two columns at separation 1/2.

Compared the exact revision with the frozen bytes. The statement, declared dependencies, source locators and source hashes are unchanged. Only the determinant citation scope and the independent interval calculation changed.

For N=2, the barycentric coordinate on B has slope of absolute value 1/|B|. The midpoint interval has length |C|/2=|B|/2, so the two column coordinate values differ by 1/2, the absolute determinant of those columns. The sum of their row maxima is consequently 3/2 and one is at least 3/4=b+δ.

The actual convex bodies A and C are positive and compact. Brunn–Minkowski gives a≤V=|C|, and each barycentric functional is nonconstant. Substitute f=λ_i and s=b_i and minimize the all-tilt inequality.
